https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/andrew-tate-ro.text: Andrew Tate has claimed that conditions inside his Miami detention cell have deteriorated, alleging he is living without hot water or air conditioning and seeing 10 to 15 cockroaches on the walls and ceiling at a time.The 39-year-old social media influencer and former professional kickboxer made the claims in a lengthy post on X, saying he had spent 61 days in the Special Housing Unit (SHU) at the Federal Detention Center in Miami.Tate said he had been moved to another cell within the same unit and described it as worse than his previous accommodation. He also said he was preparing legal action over what he described as unlawful and deliberately degrading treatment.Tate Describes His New CellTate alleged that his new cell has no hot water or air conditioning and claimed there was a 'serious roach infestation'. He said he could see 10 to 15 roaches on the ceiling and walls at any one time, despite trying to kill them. He also described the water as 'stone-cold' and the cell as filthy.Tate characterised the SHU as a punitive unit for prisoners who attack other inmates or guards, although that description comes from Tate and has not been independently established in his post. He claimed he had spent 61 days in the unit while other prisoners were released into the general population after shorter periods.Tate Says His Treatment Is DeliberateThe influencer also alleged that senior staff at the facility were deliberately treating him differently from other prisoners. Tate claimed some members of staff had told him they believed his conditions were unfair, while alleging that senior officials had refused to speak with him. He also described an incident in which officers allegedly entered a recreation area and handcuffed him and his brother, Tristan Tate.He characterised the treatment as a violation of his civil rights and called it 'cruel and unusual punishment.' Those are Tate's claims and have not been established as findings against the detention centre.Tate Remains in Custody During Extradition FightTate and his brother Tristan have been held at the Federal Detention Center in Miami since their arrest by the US Marshals Service on 18 July, after UK authorities sought their extradition. A US magistrate judge denied the brothers' request for release on 9 September, meaning they remain in custody while the extradition proceedings continue.The Crown Prosecution Service has requested their extradition to the UK. It says Andrew Tate faces further allegations including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault occasioning actual bodily harm, and offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.The CPS says the alleged offending took place between July 2010 and August 2017. Tate and his brother deny wrongdoing, and the CPS has stressed that the proceedings are active and that the defendants have the right to a fair trial.Tate Threatens Legal Action Over Jail ConditionsTate said he had prepared a package for his legal and public relations teams containing what he described as evidence of 'corruption', inadequate recreation, filth, and unsanitary conditions at the facility. He said he intended to take legal action against FDC Miami and asked people who had previously complained about the facility to contact his legal team.Tate also compared his current detention with his previous imprisonment in Romania, saying: 'The Romanians treated me better than this.' His latest claims concern conditions inside the Miami detention centre and should not be treated as independently verified facts unless supported by records or statements from the facility.What Happens Next in the Extradition CaseThe immediate issue for Tate and his brother is their ongoing extradition fight. The CPS has formally stated that it has requested their extradition from the US and that the brothers are awaiting extradition proceedings. The process will determine whether they are surrendered to UK authorities to face the allegations.For now, Tate remains in US custody, while his claims about conditions at FDC Miami are being presented by him as part of a potential legal challenge.

https://www.thefastmode.com/technology-s.text: Technologies Services Business Devices TFM Awards 2026 LiveX 27 Yettel Intros Zoho Platform to Help Businesses Integrate Sales, Marketing & HR Operations Tuesday, 10 November 2026 01:25 Ray Sharma 1 2 3 4 5 (0 votes) 4 min read font size decrease font size increase font size Comment Yettel is expanding its enterprise ICT portfolio with a Zoho-powered cloud platform that integrates sales, marketing and human resources operations, helping businesses streamline workflows, reduce administrative workloads and improve operational efficiency. The solution addresses a common challenge among businesses undergoing digital transformation: disconnected software systems that require employees to manually transfer and duplicate data. These fragmented workflows slow operations, increase the risk of errors and limit management visibility, making timely business decisions more difficult. As the Hungarian partner of international software provider Zoho, Yettel will offer businesses a customizable platform that connects individual business processes through a shared database. Companies can introduce the solution gradually, starting with the business function that requires the most attention before integrating additional departments without replacing their entire IT infrastructure. The platform also addresses data security and regulatory requirements. Zoho stores European customers' data in EU-based data centers and supports data management in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Selected modules also incorporate Zia, Zoho's artificial intelligence assistant, which can analyze sales and customer management data, recommend task priorities and provide managers with insights into daily business operations. Among the platform's key offerings is Zoho CRM, which consolidates customer information and sales activities into a single interface, covering the customer journey from initial enquiries to contract completion. Its marketing tools support the planning, distribution and measurement of email and social media campaigns, while HR applications simplify employee administration, including recruitment and leave management. For businesses seeking broader integration, Zoho One offers a comprehensive subscription covering 45 modules across more than six application areas, enabling companies to manage much of their operations within a single software ecosystem. The platform is particularly suited to growing businesses that have outgrown their existing IT systems and need greater integration across departments. Start-ups can also use the solution to establish a digital operating environment from the outset, adding applications as their operational requirements expand. Integrated Software Implementation and Support Beyond providing software licences, Yettel will deliver the Zoho platform as an end-to-end service covering business consultancy, solution selection, implementation and ongoing technical support. The company will work with customers to identify their operational requirements and recommend suitable technology solutions based on their business processes. Customers will also receive professional support in Hungarian and access to dedicated contacts throughout implementation and daily operations. Expanding Beyond Traditional Telecommunications Services The Zoho introduction forms part of Yettel's broader strategy to strengthen its position in the enterprise ICT market beyond its traditional telecommunications business. It follows the recent introduction of UiPath, a software platform that uses robotic process automation to handle repetitive administrative tasks. While UiPath focuses on automating routine activities, Zoho is intended to connect business processes and data across different departments. Gábor Fülöp, Yettel's Business Sales and Marketing Director The technological needs of companies are now driven by specific business problems. We support our customers in finding the solutions that best suit their goals, and we stand by them as a reliable partner in implementation and operation. Our goal is for Yettel to be seen as a long-term, reliable technology partner in ICT developments, in addition to the usual mobile network services. yettel zoho Ray Sharma is an Industry Analyst and Editor at The Fast Mode.
